newsitem.title: USA: US High Court denies state hazardous waste appeal.
newsitem.headline: US High Court denies state hazardous waste appeal.

text.p: The U.S. Supreme Court Monday denied South Carolina's appeal of a ruling that struck down laws restricting the amount of hazardous waste that can be brought in from other states.

The laws, adopted in 1989 and 1990, establish limits on how much out-of-state waste can be buried in South Carolina each year, bar certain out-of-state wastes, set quota preferences for in-state waste and require a special "needs" permit to create or expand a hazardous waste treatment facility.

The laws were challenged in court by a group called the Environmental Technology Council, which represents companies involved in the recycling, treatment, storage and disposal of hazardous and non-hazardous wastes.
A U.S. Court of Appeals last year struck down the laws on the grounds that they unconstitutionally discriminate against interstate commerce.
South Carolina appealed to the Supreme Court, asking the justices to hear the case. But the high court rejected the appeal without any comment or dissent.
